= BITwiki Semantic Patterns: Recurring Knowledge Structures =

== Purpose ==

This document catalogs recurring semantic patterns observed in knowledge organization. Patterns represent solutions that have emerged from practice—approaches that tend to work well, offered as guidance rather than prescription.

Patterns are not rules but observations. They evolve as knowledge practices develop.

== What Are Semantic Patterns? ==

Knowledge organizes itself into recurring structures. The same patterns appear across domains: hierarchies, causal chains, temporal sequences, dependency networks. Recognizing these patterns enables consistent knowledge representation and powerful cross-domain queries.

BITwiki patterns are not prescriptive rules but observed regularities. They emerge from how knowledge actually structures itself, not from top-down imposition.

== Pattern Categories ==

=== 1. Structural Patterns ===

==== Pattern 1.1: Entity-Attribute-Value (EAV) ====

'''Structure:''' Entity → Attribute → Value

'''Description:''' Flexible property assignment. Any entity can have any attribute with any value, enabling rich description without rigid schema.

'''Purpose:''' Flexible property assignment

'''Example:'''
```
Project: Apollo Program
├── Attribute: Cost
│   └── Value: $25.4 billion
├── Attribute: Duration
│   └── Value: 11 years
└── Attribute: Outcome
    └── Value: Lunar landing
```

'''SMW:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Project]]
[[Has cost::$25.4 billion]]
[[Has duration::11 years]]
[[Has outcome::Lunar landing]]
```

'''Simple SMW:''' [[Has age::30]]

==== Pattern 1.2: Type Hierarchy ====

'''Structure:''' General → Specific → Instance

'''Description:''' Knowledge organizes taxonomically. General categories contain specific subcategories which contain instances. This is not rigid classification but flexible navigation—entities may belong to multiple hierarchies.

'''Purpose:''' Taxonomic organization

'''Example:'''
```
Systems Science
├── Cybernetics
│ ├── First-Order Cybernetics
│ └── Second-Order Cybernetics
└── Information Theory
    └── Channel Capacity
```

'''SMW:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Topic]]
[[Is a::Systems Science]]
[[Has subtopic::Cybernetics]]
```

'''Simple SMW:''' [[Is a::Mammal]]

'''Query:''' "All topics that are subtopics of Cybernetics"

==== Pattern 1.3: Part-Whole ====

'''Structure:''' Part → Whole

'''Description:''' Mereological relationships—how components compose systems. Parts may be physical (neurons in brain) or abstract (functions in algorithm).

'''Purpose:''' Mereological relationships

'''Example:'''
```
Neural Network
├── Layers
│ ├── Input layer
│ ├── Hidden layers
│ └── Output layer
├── Neurons
└── Connections (weights)
```

'''SMW:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Implementation]]
[[Part of::Neural Network]]
[[Has part::Neuron]]
```

'''Simple SMW:''' [[Part of::Car]]

'''Query:''' "All parts of systems that implement feedback"

=== 2. Relational Patterns ===

==== Pattern 2.1: Causal Chain ====

'''Structure:''' Cause → Effect → Consequence

'''Description:''' Causal relationships propagate through systems. Understanding causal chains enables prediction and intervention.

'''Purpose:''' Causal reasoning

'''Example:'''
```
Increased CO2 → Global warming → Sea level rise → Coastal displacement
```

'''SMW:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Causes::Global warming]]
[[Has consequence::Sea level rise]]
```

'''Simple SMW:''' [[Causes::Effect]]

'''Query:''' "All effects of increased CO2 with confidence >0.8"

==== Pattern 2.2: Temporal Sequence ====

'''Structure:''' Before → During → After

'''Description:''' Temporal ordering constrains possibility. Some things must happen before others.

'''Purpose:''' Temporal reasoning

'''Example:'''
```
Problem definition → Hypothesis formation → Experiment design → Data collection → Analysis → Publication
```

'''SMW:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Protocol]]
[[Precedes::Hypothesis formation]]
[[Follows::Observation]]
```

'''Simple SMW:''' [[Precedes::Execution]]

'''Query:''' "All protocols that precede data collection"

==== Pattern 2.3: Dependency Network ====

'''Structure:''' A depends on B depends on C

'''Description:''' Dependencies create constraint networks. Changes to dependencies propagate through the network.

'''Purpose:''' Dependency tracking

'''Example:'''
```
Machine Learning Application
├── Depends on: Framework (PyTorch)
│   └── Depends on: Language (Python)
│       └── Depends on: Interpreter (CPython)
└── Depends on: Hardware (GPU)
    └── Depends on: Manufacturing (TSMC)
```

'''SMW:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Implementation]]
[[Depends on::PyTorch]]
[[Depends on::CUDA]]
```

'''Simple SMW:''' [[Depends on::Framework]]

'''Query:''' "All implementations that depend on Python"

=== 3. Epistemic Patterns ===

==== Pattern 3.1: Evidence Hierarchy ====

'''Structure:''' Hypothesis → Evidence → Confirmation

'''Description:''' Claims require support. Evidence quality varies—anecdote < observation < experiment < meta-analysis.

'''Purpose:''' Epistemic validation

'''Example:'''
```
Hypothesis: Meditation reduces stress
├── Evidence: Self-report (low quality)
├── Evidence: Cortisol measurement (medium quality)
└── Evidence: fMRI meta-analysis (high quality)
    └── Confirmation: Verified
```

'''SMW:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Supported by::Meta-analysis of 163 studies]]
[[Has epistemic status::Verified]]
[[Has confidence score::0.85]]
```

'''Simple SMW:''' [[Supported by::Evidence]]

==== Pattern 3.2: Confidence Calibration ====

'''Structure:''' Claim → Confidence → Justification

'''Description:''' Uncertainty is quantifiable. Confidence scores should match evidence strength.

'''Purpose:''' Uncertainty management

'''Example:'''
```
Claim: Climate change is anthropogenic
├── Confidence: 0.99
└── Justification: IPCC AR6, 234 authors, 14,000+ references
```

'''SMW:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Has confidence score::0.99]]
[[Has confidence justification::IPCC AR6 synthesis]]
```

'''Simple SMW:''' [[Has confidence score::0.8]]

==== Pattern 3.3: Provenance Chain ====

'''Structure:''' Origin → Transmission → Current

'''Description:''' Knowledge has history. Understanding where claims come from enables assessment of reliability.

'''Purpose:''' Source tracking

'''Example:'''
```
Original research (1972) → Peer-reviewed publication → Textbook citation → Wikipedia article → Current understanding
```

'''SMW:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Has originator::Gregory Bateson]]
[[Has source::Steps to an Ecology of Mind]]
[[Has transmission::Cited in 500+ works]]
```

'''Simple SMW:''' [[Has originator::Researcher]]

'''Query:''' "All ideas with provenance traceable to Macy Conferences"

=== 4. Recursive Patterns ===

==== Pattern 4.1: Self-Description ====

'''Structure:''' System describes itself

'''Description:''' Meta-knowledge—knowledge about the knowledge system itself. BITwiki documents BITwiki.

'''Purpose:''' Meta-knowledge

'''Example:'''
```
This document (BITwiki Semantic Patterns) is an instance of the patterns it describes.
```

'''SMW:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Documentation]]
[[Documents::BITwiki]]
[[Instance of::Semantic Pattern]]
```

'''Simple SMW:''' [[Has page type::Documentation]]

==== Pattern 4.2: Self-Validation ====

'''Structure:''' System validates its own outputs

'''Description:''' Quality control applied to the system itself. Validation rules check that BITwiki content follows BITwiki standards.

'''Purpose:''' Quality assurance

'''Example:'''
```
Validation rule: All ideas must have epistemic status
Applied to: This document
Result: Pass (has status: Established)
```

'''SMW:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Protocol]]
[[Validates::BITwiki content]]
[[Has validation target::Self]]
```

'''Simple SMW:''' [[Has validation status::Validated]]

==== Pattern 4.3: Self-Improvement ====

'''Structure:''' System improves itself

'''Description:''' Continuous refinement through recursive upgrade protocols.

'''Purpose:''' Continuous refinement

'''Example:'''
```
Recursive upgrade protocols
```

'''SMW:''' [[Has improvement cycle::Active]]

== Pattern Combinations ==

Real knowledge structures combine multiple patterns:

=== Scientific Publication ===
* Temporal sequence (research → writing → review → publication)
* Dependency network (builds on prior work)
* Evidence hierarchy (supports claims)
* Provenance chain (attribution)

=== Software Project ===
* Type hierarchy (language → framework → application)
* Part-whole (modules, functions, lines)
* Dependency network (libraries, services)
* Temporal sequence (planning → development → deployment)

Recognizing these combinations enables rich, multi-dimensional knowledge representation.

== Anti-Patterns ==

=== Anti-Pattern 1: Orphaned Entity ===

'''Problem:''' Entity with no relationships
'''Detection:''' No incoming or outgoing properties
'''Solution:''' Add relationships or remove

=== Anti-Pattern 2: Circular Definition ====

'''Problem:''' A defined in terms of B, B in terms of A
'''Detection:''' Graph cycle in definitions
'''Solution:''' Break cycle, identify base concept

=== Anti-Pattern 3: Property Bloat ====

'''Problem:''' Too many properties on single entity
'''Detection:''' >20 properties
'''Solution:''' Split into related entities

=== Anti-Pattern 4: Type Confusion ====

'''Problem:''' Entity with conflicting types
'''Detection:''' Multiple type assignments
'''Solution:''' Clarify type hierarchy

== Best Practices ==

=== Practice 1: Consistent Naming ===
* Use standard property names
* Follow naming conventions
* Document abbreviations

=== Practice 2: Explicit Relationships ====
* Declare all relationships
* Use inverse properties
* Document semantics

=== Practice 3: Minimal Redundancy ====
* Store data once
* Use transclusion for reuse
* Avoid duplication

=== Practice 4: Query Optimization ====
* Index frequently queried properties
* Use efficient query patterns
* Cache results

== SMW Implementation ==

=== Pattern Properties ===

```wiki
[[Has pattern type::Structural]]
[[Has pattern name::EAV]]
[[Has anti-pattern::Orphaned Entity]]
[[Has best practice::Consistent Naming]]
```

=== Pattern Queries ===

'''All structural patterns:'''
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has pattern type::Structural]]}}
```

'''Patterns with anti-patterns:'''
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has anti-pattern::+]]}}
```

== On Pattern Evolution ==

Patterns emerge from practice, not theory. They represent what has worked, not what must work. As knowledge practices evolve, new patterns will emerge and existing patterns may become obsolete.

The patterns here are offered as guidance—tools that have proven useful, not constraints that must be followed.

== References ==

# Gamma, E., et al. (1994). Design Patterns.
# Fowler, M. (2002). Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture.
# Semantic MediaWiki. (2026).
# W3C. (2014). RDF Schema 1.1.
# OWL 2 Web Ontology Language. (2012).
# BITwiki Ontology Index. (2026).
# BITwiki Constitution. (2026).
# Sowa, J.F. (2000). Knowledge Representation.
# Noy, N.F., & McGuinness, D.L. (2001). Ontology development 101.
# Gruber, T.R. (1993). A translation approach to portable ontology specifications.

=== 2. Relational Patterns ===

==== Pattern 2.1: Causal Chain ====

'''Structure:''' Cause → Effect → Consequence

'''Description:''' Causal relationships propagate through systems. Understanding causal chains enables prediction and intervention.

'''Purpose:''' Causal reasoning

'''Example:'''
```
Increased CO2 → Global warming → Sea level rise → Coastal displacement
```

'''SMW:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Causes::Global warming]]
[[Has consequence::Sea level rise]]
```

'''Simple SMW:''' [[Causes::Effect]]

'''Query:''' "All effects of increased CO2 with confidence >0.8"

==== Pattern 2.2: Temporal Sequence ====

'''Structure:''' Before → During → After

'''Description:''' Temporal ordering constrains possibility. Some things must happen before others.

'''Purpose:''' Temporal reasoning

'''Example:'''
```
Problem definition → Hypothesis formation → Experiment design → Data collection → Analysis → Publication
```

'''SMW:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Protocol]]
[[Precedes::Hypothesis formation]]
[[Follows::Observation]]
```

'''Simple SMW:''' [[Precedes::Execution]]

'''Query:''' "All protocols that precede data collection"

==== Pattern 2.3: Dependency Network ====

'''Structure:''' A depends on B depends on C

'''Description:''' Dependencies create constraint networks. Changes to dependencies propagate through the network.

'''Purpose:''' Dependency tracking

'''Example:'''
```
Machine Learning Application
├── Depends on: Framework (PyTorch)
│   └── Depends on: Language (Python)
│       └── Depends on: Interpreter (CPython)
└── Depends on: Hardware (GPU)
    └── Depends on: Manufacturing (TSMC)
```

'''SMW:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Implementation]]
[[Depends on::PyTorch]]
[[Depends on::CUDA]]
```

'''Simple SMW:''' [[Depends on::Framework]]

'''Query:''' "All implementations that depend on Python"

=== 3. Epistemic Patterns ===

==== Pattern 3.1: Evidence Hierarchy ====

'''Structure:''' Hypothesis → Evidence → Confirmation

'''Description:''' Claims require support. Evidence quality varies—anecdote < observation < experiment < meta-analysis.

'''Purpose:''' Epistemic validation

'''Example:'''
```
Hypothesis: Meditation reduces stress
├── Evidence: Self-report (low quality)
├── Evidence: Cortisol measurement (medium quality)
└── Evidence: fMRI meta-analysis (high quality)
    └── Confirmation: Verified
```

'''SMW:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Supported by::Meta-analysis of 163 studies]]
[[Has epistemic status::Verified]]
[[Has confidence score::0.85]]
```

'''Simple SMW:''' [[Supported by::Evidence]]

==== Pattern 3.2: Confidence Calibration ====

'''Structure:''' Claim → Confidence → Justification

'''Description:''' Uncertainty is quantifiable. Confidence scores should match evidence strength.

'''Purpose:''' Uncertainty management

'''Example:'''
```
Claim: Climate change is anthropogenic
├── Confidence: 0.99
└── Justification: IPCC AR6, 234 authors, 14,000+ references
```

'''SMW:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Has confidence score::0.99]]
[[Has confidence justification::IPCC AR6 synthesis]]
```

'''Simple SMW:''' [[Has confidence score::0.8]]

==== Pattern 3.3: Provenance Chain ====

'''Structure:''' Origin → Transmission → Current

'''Description:''' Knowledge has history. Understanding where claims come from enables assessment of reliability.

'''Purpose:''' Source tracking

'''Example:'''
```
Original research (1972) → Peer-reviewed publication → Textbook citation → Wikipedia article → Current understanding
```

'''SMW:'''
```wiki

[[Has originator::Gregory Bateson]]
[[Has source::Steps to an Ecology of Mind]]

```

== Pattern Combinations ==

Real knowledge structures combine multiple patterns:

=== Scientific Publication ===
* Temporal sequence (research → writing → review → publication)
* Dependency network (builds on prior work)
* Evidence hierarchy (supports claims)
* Provenance chain (attribution)

=== Software Project ===
* Type hierarchy (language → framework → application)
* Part-whole (modules, functions, lines)
* Dependency network (libraries, services)
* Temporal sequence (planning → development → deployment)

Recognizing these combinations enables rich, multi-dimensional knowledge representation.

== Anti-Patterns ==

=== Anti-Pattern 1: Orphaned Entity ===

'''Problem:''' Entity with no relationships
'''Detection:''' No incoming or outgoing properties
'''Solution:''' Add relationships or remove

=== Anti-Pattern 2: Circular Definition ====

'''Problem:''' A defined in terms of B, B in terms of A
'''Detection:''' Graph cycle in definitions
'''Solution:''' Break cycle, identify base concept

=== Anti-Pattern 3: Property Bloat ====

'''Problem:''' Too many properties on single entity
'''Detection:''' >20 properties
'''Solution:''' Split into related entities

=== Anti-Pattern 4: Type Confusion ====

'''Problem:''' Entity with conflicting types
'''Detection:''' Multiple type assignments
'''Solution:''' Clarify type hierarchy

== Best Practices ==

=== Practice 1: Consistent Naming ===
* Use standard property names
* Follow naming conventions
* Document abbreviations

=== Practice 2: Explicit Relationships ====
* Declare all relationships
* Use inverse properties
* Document semantics

=== Practice 3: Minimal Redundancy ====
* Store data once
* Use transclusion for reuse
* Avoid duplication

=== Practice 4: Query Optimization ====
* Index frequently queried properties
* Use efficient query patterns
* Cache results

== On Pattern Evolution ==

Patterns emerge from practice, not theory. They represent what has worked, not what must work. As knowledge practices evolve, new patterns will emerge and existing patterns may become obsolete.

The patterns here are offered as guidance—tools that have proven useful, not constraints that must be followed.
